lessons.title: का (kā) — why
lessons.gloss: why — the same syllable as the question particle, moved to the front of the sentence

segments.text: Retrieve the two items before this one by name: the particle का that turns a statement into a yes-or-no question, and the single? that marks it on the page. Say a question with both.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: का at the front

segments.text: का? — kā? — why?
का आवडते? — kā āvaḍte? — Why do you like it?

The same two letters you have just learned to hang on the end mean why when they stand at the front, or on their own. That is not a coincidence and it is not an accident of spelling: both come from the Sanskrit question stem क- (ka-), (svalpaviraam) which also built काय ("what") and कसा ("how"). Marathi's whole question system is one syllable with different tails, and the same Indo-European k- is under Latin quis and English who.
Position is what keeps the two apart, so it is worth saying both aloud back to back:
मराठी आवडते का? — do you like Marathi? (particle, at the end).
मराठी का आवडते? — why do you like Marathi? (question word, in front of the verb).
Said on its own, का? is a complete turn: it is how you ask someone to explain what they have just said.

segments.instruction: marāṭhī āvaḍte kā? then marāṭhī kā āvaḍte?
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *marāṭhī āvaḍte kā?* then *marāṭhī kā āvaḍte?*]

segments.instruction: kā? on its own, as a whole turn
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *kā?* on its own, as a whole turn]

segments.instruction: the three k-words together — kāy, kasā, kā

segments.prompt: Ask whether the listener likes Marathi, then ask why — the same word in two positions.
acceptedResponses: marāṭhī āvaḍte kā? — marāṭhī kā āvaḍte?
मराठी आवडते का? मराठी का आवडते?

feedback.correct: End means yes-or-no; front means why.
feedback.incorrect: Move का to the front and the question changes kind.

segments.text: What does का mean at the front of a sentence? (Why.) And at the end? (It makes a yes-or-no question.) What decides which? (Where it stands.)
Sources: Wiktionary: का.

lessons.title: कारण (kāraṇ) — because
lessons.gloss: because — the word that answers का, and the first joiner that puts a whole clause after it

segments.text: You can now ask का?. Ask it out loud. Then notice that you have no way whatever to answer it.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: कारण takes a whole sentence after it

segments.text: मी मराठी शिकतो कारण मला मराठी आवडते. — mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte. — I am learning Marathi because I like Marathi.

आणि, किंवा and पण put two things side by side as equals. कारण (kāraṇ) does something new: everything after it is subordinate — it exists only to explain the half in front. That is the first time in this book that one Marathi clause has been put inside the job of another.
The order is fixed and it is the useful way round: the claim first, the reason second. English can lead with because; Marathi's ordinary sentence does not.

कारण is Sanskrit कारण (kāraṇa), (svalpaviraam) "a cause," built on the root कृ (kṛ-), (svalpaviraam) "to do" — the same कृ inside करणे, the verb this book gave you for to do. Marathi's because is, at root, the doing of it.
A short answer works too. Asked का?, (svalpaviraam) you may reply with कारण (kāraṇ) and one clause, and nothing else is needed.

segments.instruction: kā? then answer it with kāraṇ …
malā chahā āvaḍto paṇ dūdh āvaḍat nāhī — equals — then mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte — not equals
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *malā chahā āvaḍto paṇ dūdh āvaḍat nāhī* — equals — then *mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte* — not equals]

segments.instruction: which verb कारण (kāraṇ) is related to — karṇe
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which verb **कारण** is related to — *karṇe*]

segments.prompt: Ask why, then answer with a reason: you are learning Marathi because you like it.
acceptedResponses: kā? — mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte
का? मी मराठी शिकतो कारण मला मराठी आवडते

feedback.incorrect: Put the claim first and kāraṇ in front of the reason.

segments.text: Which half comes first in a Marathi कारण (kāraṇ) sentence? (The claim; the reason follows.) How is कारण (kāraṇ) unlike पण? (पण joins two equals; कारण (kāraṇ) puts one clause underneath the other.)
Sources: Wiktionary: कारण (kāraṇ).

lessons.title: , (svalpaviraam) — the mark that carries a list
lessons.gloss: the comma — the mark that separates a list on the page where आणि separates it in the mouth

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
waitUntilStopped: Script: the comma does the joining work for all but the last pair
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script: the comma does the joining work for all but the last pair until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Say चहा आणि दूध आणि पाणी. Three things, two आणि. Out loud it is clumsy; on paper it is worse.

blocks.title: Script: the comma does the joining work for all but the last pair

segments.text: चहा, दूध आणि पाणी.

Marathi writes the comma exactly as English does: it stands in for the joining word between every pair except the last, where आणि is written out. The mark is the same shape you already know from the Latin alphabet, sitting on the baseline below the letters — not hanging from the headline like a Devanagari sign.
It has one more everyday job, and it is the one the writing task needs:
नमस्कार मीरा, मी अरुण. — namaskār Mīrā, mī Aruṇ.
A comma after the person you are addressing. Every message that opens by naming its reader wants one.
Marathi's own name for it, स्वल्पविराम, means "small pause," which is a better description than comma — the mark tells the eye to hesitate, not to stop.
Write चहा, दूध आणि पाणी once. Then write नमस्कार मीरा, and check that the comma sits on the baseline, after the name.

segments.prompt: Write the three drinks as one written list, using the comma and one āṇi.

feedback.correct: Comma between the first pair, āṇi before the last.
feedback.incorrect: Only the LAST pair keeps āṇi; the rest take commas.

segments.text: In a written list of three, how many आणि do you write, and where? (One, before the last item.) What does the comma's Marathi name mean? (Small pause.)

lessons.title: Two turns: why, and because
lessons.gloss: asking for a reason and giving one, in two turns

segments.text: का at the end asks yes-or-no. का at the front asks why. Say one of each before you go on.

segments.instruction: marāṭhī āvaḍte kā? — ho — kā? — kāraṇ …
mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte*]

segments.prompt: Take both turns: ask why, then answer with a reason.
acceptedResponses: kā? — mī marāṭhī shikto kāraṇ malā marāṭhī āvaḍte
का? मी मराठी शिकतो कारण मला मराठी आवडते

feedback.correct: A question and a reason: the smallest complete exchange in the book.
feedback.incorrect: Ask kā?, then answer with the claim first and kāraṇ before the reason.

segments.text: Which joining word puts one clause underneath another? (कारण (kāraṇ).) Which half of a कारण (kāraṇ) sentence comes first? (The claim.) Then stop.
